headline: Commercial coral farming grows climate-resilient reefs 50 times faster
meta_description: Commercial coral farms use microfragmentation and controlled conditions to grow climate-resilient corals on land 50 times faster than nature, offering new hope…
summary_short: Coral farms are now growing climate-resilient corals on land at rates 50 times faster than nature, using controlled water conditions and microfragmentation techniques.
body:
Commercial coral farming is accelerating reef restoration by growing climate-resilient corals on land 50 times faster than nature can.

The breakthrough relies on precise control over three critical factors: water temperature, water chemistry, and light conditions. By maintaining these parameters in optimized ways, farmers create an environment where corals thrive far beyond their natural pace.

Microfragmentation—a technique that divides coral colonies into smaller pieces—amplifies this speed advantage, allowing a single parent colony to generate many more offspring for planting. These lab-grown corals show greater resilience to climate stress, offering a practical tool for restoring damaged reefs before warming oceans destroy them entirely. As reefs worldwide face unprecedented pressure from ocean acidification and temperature rise, this commercial approach bridges the gap between conservation urgency and nature's slower timelines.
quick_facts: Corals grown on land, 50 times faster than wild growth
Controlled water temperature, chemistry, and light conditions
Microfragmentation technique multiplies coral offspring rapidly
